task.problem:
Let X be connected and compact, of complex dimension n>=2, with dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial and a smooth positive probability volume dV. All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, not arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications. Extended Monge-Ampere measures are the non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C; ordinary equivalence u~v means mutual inequalities up to finite constants, interpreted canonically at common poles. For a Hermitian metric h and nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), b_h(f)=lim_k c_h(min(f,k)), where c_h(g)>0 is the scalar of the supremum-normalized continuous bounded-density equation. It is equivalently the maximal a>=0 for a genuine subsolution MA_ext_h(u)>=a f dV. The attained subsolution can have excess or infinite mass. Define v_-(h)=inf integral(h+dd^c u)^n over all bounded genuine h-psh u. For a smooth big real (1,1) form theta, P_theta(a) is the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh potentials <=a. Define P_(theta,F)[u] as the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=F with v preceq u; P_theta[u] uses F=0. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,phi) consists of u preceq phi such that for every t>=1 some genuine theta-psh a satisfies t^(-1)a+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u. This stretching definition is meaningful at common poles. Do not silently replace it by envelope equality without the additional hypotheses proving an equivalence. Fix an effective real divisor E=sum a_j E_j, a_j>=0, and a smooth closed Bott-Chern representative beta_E, with [E]=beta_E+dd^c ell_E for its canonical logarithmic potential. Normalize every smooth positive Gauduchon (n-1,n-1) test T by dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. Its determinant density is k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n) for T=gamma^(n-1). Set p=f^(1/n) and D_p(T)=integral p k_T dV; the full smooth-test supremum is b_h(f)^(-1/n) when b_h(f)>0. The linear threshold kappa_h(beta_E) is inf over these smooth tests of integral beta_E wedge T. Let C_h be their weak closure, not all normalized positive dd^c-closed currents. The annihilating face is {T in C_h:integral beta_E wedge T=0}. For singular T this smooth class pairing does not define [E] wedge T. Known necessary facts: if MA_ext_h(u)>=c f dV with c>0 and h+dd^c u>=[E], then c<=b_h(f)(1-kappa_h(beta_E))^n, with 0<=kappa_h(beta_E)<1. At c=b_h(f), every smooth maximizing sequence annihilates beta_E in the limit. Uniform integrability of the densities p k_(T_j) guarantees that its cluster currents actually maximize. The weak closure of smooth tests can be strictly smaller than all normalized Gauduchon currents, even on a Kahler blowup. Further known exclusions: a semipositive beta_E with f giving no mass to its zero locus excludes a threshold component when such uniform integrability is available. Under the same uniform-integrability hypothesis, a nef divisor component at threshold must have zero fixed-density variational volume. In particular the standard Hopf hyperplane cannot occur in a threshold subsolution for any nonzero L1 density, despite zero variational volume of its class. These are necessary conditions and exclusions, not inverse realization. Original S12 asks for sufficient conditions converting the annihilating data into an actual threshold subsolution with h+dd^c u>=[E]. Separately, define and characterize the maximal coefficient restricted to one specified ordinary or relative envelope type. A global threshold need not equal the restricted threshold; specify the reference, class, admissibility and whether a supremum is attained. No candidate inverse construction, divisor, density family or proof is supplied.

imposed on the initially proposed E. Keep actual current domination;

mass. This is a smooth-data obstruction, not general L1 inverse realization.

The global threshold b_H(R)=CV0 while all three restricted thresholds

If v_-(h0)=0, prove v_-(H)=v_-(H_E)=0 and both backgrounds nonclosed;
